primary_sources_read.finding: Actual held cover/title and 2015 year verified. Nielsen moves/rank/source tree actions at physical 14–16,26–31; question contexts at physical 16,19,33,35,51,56,80–81.

Myropolska–Nagnibeda primary describes Nielsen graphs and transitivity/nonamenability. Source statements in this packet distinguish rank Nielsen classes from Andrews–Curtis classes, abstract group automorphisms, and graph expansion.

Myropolska primary structural characterizations of MN and examples; [G,G]≤Φ(G), all finite quotients nilpotent, and solvable/linear cases do not construct an exponential-growth group in the full MN class.

Current 2026 published GGD primary provides criteria for certain constant spinal torsion groups to have only finite-index maximal subgroups, and examples outside that class. This is proper partial classification, not all finitely generated branch groups. Torsion does not alone characterize the class.

Current 2026 primary derived-series/Frattini structure of GGS groups. It mentions a family containing some intermediate-growth examples, not proof that the specific Gupta–Sidki recursion below has intermediate word growth for all odd primes.

2026 primary thesis abstract read: generalizes infinite Nielsen classes of torsion GGS generating pairs and counts Andrews–Curtis classes for nonconstant defining vectors. Those results differ from first Grigorchuk generating triples and the finite-level Gupta–Sidki Nielsen-class count sequence.

Kofinas (2024), Remark 1(1), explicitly identifies the exact centre-by-metabelian group G_(n,1)=F_n/[F_n″,F_n] and states that its extra automorphism is non-tame for every n≥4, citing reference [5], Bryant–Gupta–Levin–Mochizuki (1990). This negatively answers the source tameness question. The k≥2 main theorem concerns another family and is not needed for this closure.

2025/2026 primary small-Ree Wiegold result is a proper finite simple-family result. It does not prove connectivity for every finite G and n≥d(G)+1. Wiegold normal-rank/perfect-group results have a different predicate.

Nitsche primary proves property(T) for Aut(F4); higher ranks were already proved by Kaluba–Nowak–Ozawa/Kielak. Historical source property(T) question is solved and excluded; no new Nielsen target is invented from that historical sentence.

accepted.title: Finite-group Nielsen connectivity with one extra generator
accepted.text: For a group G and n≥d(G), where d(G) is the minimum size of a generating set, let N_n(G) have vertices all ordered generating n-tuples. Join tuples related by inversion of an entry or by replacing g_i with g_i g_j^{±1} or g_j^{±1}g_i for i≠j. Its connected components are Nielsen-equivalence classes, equivalently the orbits of precomposition by Aut(F_n) on epimorphisms F_n→G. For every finite group G and every integer n≥d(G)+1, is N_n(G) connected?

accepted.title: Finite-index maximal subgroups in branch groups
accepted.text: For d≥2 let T_d be the rooted tree of all finite words in {1,…,d}, with an edge from w to wi. A subgroup G≤Aut(T_d) acts faithfully. For a vertex v let rist_G(v) consist of automorphisms that fix every vertex outside the subtree beginning with v; let rist_G(m) be the subgroup generated by rist_G(v) for all length-m vertices. Characterize the finitely generated groups G in the source branch class [G:rist_G(m)]<∞ for every m≥0 for which every maximal proper subgroup of G has finite index. A maximal proper subgroup M<G means there is no subgroup strictly between M and G. The characterization should cover arbitrary such G and d, not only a particular spinal recursion.

accepted.title: Growth of Nielsen-class counts in finite Gupta–Sidki quotients
accepted.text: For a group G and n≥d(G), where d(G) is the minimum size of a generating set, let N_n(G) have vertices all ordered generating n-tuples. Join tuples related by inversion of an entry or by replacing g_i with g_i g_j^{±1} or g_j^{±1}g_i for i≠j. Its connected components are Nielsen-equivalence classes, equivalently the orbits of precomposition by Aut(F_n) on epimorphisms F_n→G. For an odd prime p let G_p=⟨x,y⟩≤Aut(T_p), where T_p is the rooted tree {1,…,p}*. Let x cyclically permute the first letters 1,…,p and act trivially below them, and let y fix first letters with sections (x,x⁻¹,1,…,1,y). For p=3 this list is (x,x⁻¹,y). Let St_{G_p}(m) be the subgroup fixing every word of length m. For m≥1 put H_m=G₃/St_{G₃}(m+3), and let c_m be the number of connected components of N₂(H_m). Does c_m→∞ as m→∞?
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical 51 defines H_m with level m+3 and asks whether the number grows with m. The following sentence says a positive answer would imply infinitely many classes in G₃; unbounded growth is the disclosed interpretation, not strict increase at every successive level or merely c_m>1 (already proved). Finite quotient generating pairs lift through these p-group quotients, so the induced class maps are surjective and c_m is nondecreasing.
accepted.literature_finding: Own-source proves nontransitivity for every level and infinitely many classes in the infinite group, but its proof explicitly does not rely on finite quotient unboundedness. Current2026 GGS generating-pair result does not give this finite-level sequence; no exact unbounded-count answer found.
accepted.duplicate_review: Full live word/character neighbors, source-author/title/URL manifest aliases and whole-corpus source siblings manually compared; no exact full target found. Source repetitions merged without separate numbering; scores are retrieval only. Q2721 concerns absolute profinite rigidity of free and surface groups; it does not count Nielsen classes in Gupta–Sidki quotients. Q4040 concerns relatively free group growth and Q3778 connected graph partitions. The source infinite-group result and finite nontransitivity result are weaker and do not answer unbounded quotient counts.

accepted.title: Exponential growth with every maximal subgroup normal
accepted.text: For a finite symmetric generating set S of a group G let b_{G,S}(r) be the number of group elements expressible as a product of at most r members of S. Exponential growth means lim_{r→∞}b_{G,S}(r)^{1/r}>1; intermediate growth means b_{G,S}(r)/r^k→∞ for every k≥1 while lim_{r→∞}b_{G,S}(r)^{1/r}=1. These growth types are independent of the finite generating set. Does there exist a finitely generated group G of exponential growth for which every maximal proper subgroup M<G is normal in G? Here maximal means no subgroup lies strictly between M and G; all maximal subgroups are quantified, including those of infinite index.
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory
